title: Ontario Liberals elect Navdeep Bains as new party leader
summary: Ontario Liberals have elected Navdeep Bains as the party's new leader after a marathon nine-month leadership race, with Bains emerging as victor less than one percentage point ahead of his next…

image.caption: Navdeep Bains is taking the helm of the Ontario Liberals after party members elected him as leader. (Arlyn McAdorey/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Ontario Liberals have elected Navdeep Bains as the party's new leader after a marathon nine-month leadership race, with Bains emerging as victor less than one percentage point ahead of his next closest competitor, provincial caucus member Lee Fairclough.
Navdeep Bains is the third elected party leader since 2018
After receiving 50.3 per cent of the vote on the third and final ballot at the party's leadership convention, Bains took to the stage to thank the other candidates.
"This may be the end of a leadership race, ladies and gentlemen, but this is just the beginning of our campaign to replace Doug Ford and the [Progressive] Conservative Party of Ontario," he said.
The province's premier congratulated Bains on the win, in a post to social media platform X.

"Ontario families are counting on us to work collaboratively and put province over party so we can stand up to tariffs, protect workers and make life more affordable," Ford said. "I look forward to continuing that work."
Bains is now expected to shepherd the party into the next election, which may not come until 2030.
The provincial Liberal party has been without a long-term leader since Bonnie Crombie's resignation in January.
Bains has 13 years of political experience after representing Mississauga ridings as a Liberal MP and formerly served as the federal minister of innovation, science and industry from 2015 to 2021.
Before entering politics, he was a senior financial analyst at Ford Motor Company. After leaving parliament in 2021, he became an executive at CIBC and later at Rogers Communications.
Bains becomes the party's third leader since former premier Kathleen Wynne resigned following the party's sweeping 2018 election defeat.

Steven Del Duca was chosen as leader in 2020 but resigned two years later after a disappointing election result, and Crombie served from late 2023 until early this year, when she left following a weak leadership vote at an annual general meeting.
Bains, like Del Duca and Crombie when they were selected as leader, does not have a seat in the Ontario legislature.
Ahead of the results, interim Liberal leader John Fraser, who took on the role following Crombie's resignation, said he was excited and relieved to pass the baton.
"It's a new beginning," he told CBC News. "It's like a blank canvas. It's time for another generation to lead."
With files from The Canadian Press
